preconditions.description: The first line contains two integers V (1 ≤ V ≤ 10000) and E (0 ≤ E ≤ 200000), representing the number of vertices and edges in the graph.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 3 and 0 <= int(line.split()[0]) < V and 0 <= int(line.split()[1]) < V and 1 <= int(line.split()[2]) <= 99 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:1+E])
preconditions.description: Each of the next E lines contains three integers u, v, w (0 ≤ u, v ≤ V-1, 1 ≤ w ≤ 99) representing a directed edge from u to v with weight w.
The last line contains two integers s and t (0 ≤ s, t ≤ V-1), representing the source and destination vertices.
The input has exactly E + 2 lines: one for V and E, E lines for edges, and one for s and t.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the number of different shortest paths from s to t, fitting in a 32-bit signed integer.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == len([path for path in all_shortest_paths(s, t, parse_graph(stdin))])
postconditions.description: The output is the count of distinct shortest paths from s to t, where distinctness is defined by unique edge sets in the path.
